Change point: a step in a series and Pettitt's test

Source: R/trn.R
stpcp.Rd

Asks whether a series moved to a new level, and where. The step scan takes every split after period k with at least minseg periods on each side, and the largest between-segment sum of squares \(T_k = k (n - k) / n (\bar y_a - \bar y_b)^2\); its p-value comes from the same maximum over reorderings of the series (every ordering when n! is at most nperm, giving an exact p-value; otherwise nperm random ones, (1 + #{T* >= T}) / (1 + nperm)), so it is a test of a step anywhere, not of the best split alone. Pettitt's rank test takes the split with the largest \(|U_t|\), \(U_t = \sum_{i \le t < j} sign(y_j - y_i)\), with its approximate p-value \(2 \exp(-6 K^2 / (n^3 + n^2))\). Both assume exchangeable periods under no change: a steady trend can read as a step.

Usage

stpcp(y, x = NULL, minseg = 2, nperm = 9999, seed = NULL)

Arguments

y

The series, in period order: finite numbers.

x

NULL, or the periods (any vector, one per value): at then names the last period before each change.

minseg

The fewest periods on either side of a step: one whole number from 1.

nperm

The reorderings of the step scan's null: one whole number from 1.

seed

NULL to draw the seed from R's generator, or one whole number from 0.

Value

An object of class stpcp, a list: tab, one row for each test (test, k, the last period before the change, the means before and after, the statistic stat (T or K) and p, with at from x); nperm, the orderings used; exact; and n.

References

Pettitt, A. N. (1979). A non-parametric approach to the change-point problem. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C, 28(2), 126-135. doi:10.2307/2346729

Examples

stpcp(c(100, 104, 98, 60, 63, 58), x = 2018:2023)
#> stpcp: 6 periods; step p-value exact over 720 orderings
#>     test k   before    after     stat         p   at
#>     step 3 100.6667 60.33333 2440.167 0.1000000 2020
#>  pettitt 3 100.6667 60.33333    9.000 0.2907114 2020
stpcp(c(100, 104, 98, 101, 97, 60, 63, 58, 61, 59), nperm = 999, seed = 1)
#> stpcp: 10 periods; step p-value from 999 orderings
#>     test k before after   stat         p
#>     step 5    100  60.2 3960.1 0.0100000
#>  pettitt 5    100  60.2   25.0 0.0661425
